title: LMNT for a Hangover: Does It Work? Timing, Dose and Sodium
excerpt: Does LMNT help a hangover? What its 1,000 mg of sodium does and doesn't fix, when to drink it, how much is too much, who should skip it, and how it compares to Liquid I.V. and Pedialyte.
metaDescription: Does LMNT help a hangover? What its high sodium does and doesn't fix, when to drink it, how much is too much, and who should check with a doctor first.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** LMNT can help with the dehydration part of a hangover, and some people genuinely feel better after a glass of it. It is not a hangover cure. LMNT is a salty, sugar-free electrolyte mix with about 1,000 mg of sodium per stick, which is a lot. That high sodium is useful if you sweated heavily, threw up, or simply drank a lot and urinated a lot, but it does nothing for the other causes of a hangover, like poor sleep, inflammation, and the by-products your body makes while breaking down alcohol. And because it's so salty, it's not a great daily habit for people with high blood pressure, kidney disease, or heart problems.

**The quick rules:** If you want to use LMNT after drinking, mix one stick into a full 32 ounces of water rather than a small glass, sip it over an hour or so, and pair it with plain water and some food. Don't stack several sticks in a day "to flush it out." If you have high blood pressure or have been told to limit salt, talk to your doctor before using it, or pick a lower-sodium option.

> **This is not medical advice.** This article explains general research and label information about LMNT and hangovers. It is not a substitute for a doctor who knows your health history. **Talk to a doctor before using high-sodium electrolyte mixes if** you have high blood pressure, kidney disease, heart failure, or liver disease, you've been told to limit salt or fluids, you're pregnant, or you take medicines that affect sodium, potassium, or fluid balance (for example some blood pressure pills, water pills, lithium, or potassium-sparing drugs). **Get medical help right away if** someone who has been drinking is confused, very hard to wake, breathing slowly or irregularly, has blue-tinged or cold, clammy skin, is having a seizure, or can't stop vomiting. Those are signs of alcohol poisoning, not a hangover. In the US, call 911.

## Does LMNT Help a Hangover?

LMNT helps with one specific piece of a hangover: fluid and salt loss. Whether that piece matters much for you depends on how your night went.

Alcohol makes you pee more than you drink. It does this by lowering a hormone called vasopressin (also known as antidiuretic hormone), which normally tells your kidneys to hold on to water. With less of that signal, your kidneys let more water go. You lose some sodium and potassium along with it. If you also danced in a hot room, sweated, or vomited, you lose more fluid and more salt.

That's the situation where a salty drink makes sense. Sodium is the main electrolyte that helps your body hold on to water you drink. Plain water still rehydrates you, but if you drink a lot of it quickly, much of it can pass straight through. A bit of salt helps more of it stay.

Here's the part most product marketing leaves out. Hangover researchers have looked at whether dehydration and electrolyte levels explain how bad people feel the next morning, and the link turns out to be weak. Reviews of the hangover literature have found that blood electrolyte levels usually don't differ much between people with and without a hangover, and they don't track closely with how severe the hangover is. Dehydration explains the dry mouth, the thirst, and some of the headache and lightheadedness. It doesn't explain the nausea, the brain fog, the anxiety, or the general feeling of being run over.

So the realistic expectation is this: **LMNT can help you rehydrate a bit faster and may take the edge off thirst, a headache, or dizziness on standing. It won't fix the hangover itself.** If you were badly dehydrated, the difference can be noticeable. If you drank three beers and slept well, it probably won't do much that a glass of water and breakfast wouldn't.

For a full explanation of why drinking dries you out and how much of a hangover that really accounts for, see our guide to [whether alcohol dehydrates you](/never-hungover/does-alcohol-dehydrate-you).

## What's Actually in LMNT

LMNT is deliberately simple. Per stick, the standard flavors contain approximately:

| Ingredient | Amount per stick (approx.) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Sodium | ~1,000 mg | The main electrolyte for holding on to water |
| Potassium | ~200 mg | Works with sodium inside your cells |
| Magnesium | ~60 mg | Involved in muscle and nerve function |
| Sugar | 0 g | None |
| Sweetener | Stevia (the "Raw" version is unsweetened) | Flavor without sugar |
| Calories | Under 10 | Essentially none |

These figures come from the brand's published labels at the time of writing. Labels change, so check the current box for exact numbers.

What stands out is the ratio. LMNT has about five times as much sodium as potassium and no sugar. That's very different from most hangover-marketed drinks. Liquid I.V. has about half the sodium and adds sugar. Pedialyte has less sodium per serving than LMNT and also includes sugar. Gatorade has much less sodium and a lot more sugar.

LMNT was built for a specific audience: athletes who sweat a lot and people on low-carb or keto diets, who tend to lose more sodium through their kidneys. The company's view, shaped by co-founder Robb Wolf's background in the low-carb world, is that many active people are under-salted. That may well be true for a marathon runner in August. It's less obviously true for a typical person on a Sunday morning after a night out, since the average American diet already contains plenty of sodium.

### How salty is it, really?

Because you choose how much water to add, the useful number is concentration, not the amount in the stick.

- **One stick in 16 oz of water:** roughly 90 millimoles of sodium per liter. That's saltier than the World Health Organization's oral rehydration solution, which sits at 75, and many people find it tastes like seawater at this strength.
- **One stick in 32 oz of water:** roughly 45 millimoles per liter. That's closer to a stick of Liquid I.V. in 16 ounces and much easier to drink.

For a hangover, the 32-ounce mix is the better choice. It's gentler on a queasy stomach, and you're getting more actual water, which is the thing you're short on.

## LMNT and the Missing Sugar

One reason medical rehydration drinks contain a little glucose is that your small intestine absorbs sodium and glucose together through the same transport system, and water follows. That's the basic science behind oral rehydration solutions, which have saved huge numbers of lives in cases of severe diarrhea.

LMNT skips the sugar. That doesn't mean it can't rehydrate you. Sodium is still absorbed without glucose, and for mild dehydration in a healthy adult, a salty drink plus a meal works fine. If you eat breakfast alongside your LMNT, the food provides the carbohydrate anyway.

Where the missing sugar can matter:

- **If you're nauseated and can't eat.** A drink that has a bit of sugar gives you some energy and helps absorption. Pedialyte or a classic oral rehydration solution is the more textbook choice when you can't keep food down.
- **If you feel shaky or weak.** Heavy drinking can lower blood sugar in some people, especially if they skipped dinner. A zero-sugar drink won't help that. Some toast, fruit, or juice will. Our guide to [hangover shakes](/never-hungover/hangover-shakes) covers why that happens.

Where the missing sugar is a plus:

- **If you're watching calories or carbs.** LMNT adds essentially nothing.
- **If sweet drinks turn your stomach the morning after.** Some people find a salty, less sweet drink easier, and the unsweetened Raw version is an option.

## The Sodium Question: Who Should Be Careful

This is the most important section on this page. A single LMNT stick has about 1,000 mg of sodium. The Dietary Guidelines for Americans suggest most adults keep sodium under 2,300 mg a day, and the American Heart Association suggests an ideal limit of 1,500 mg for most adults, especially those with high blood pressure. One stick uses up a large share of that before you've eaten anything. A typical hangover breakfast (bacon, eggs, toast, maybe a breakfast sandwich) brings plenty more.

For a healthy adult who sweats a lot, that's usually fine, because they're losing some of it. For a healthy person on a quiet hangover morning, one stick is generally fine too. The concern is regular use, several sticks in one day, or use by people whose bodies don't handle extra sodium well.

**Talk to your doctor before using LMNT if you:**

- Have high blood pressure, or take medicine for it
- Have kidney disease, heart failure, or liver disease (including fluid buildup)
- Have been told to limit salt or fluids
- Take diuretics (water pills), lithium, or other medicines that change how your body handles sodium or potassium
- Are pregnant

If your doctor says a lower-sodium option is better, Liquid I.V. has about half the sodium per stick, and you can always make a simple homemade version with less salt. Our [homemade electrolyte drink guide](/never-hungover/homemade-electrolyte-drink) shows how.

### Can you have too much?

For most healthy people, one or two sticks spread through a day with plenty of water won't cause problems. Downing several sticks in a short time is not a good idea. Very concentrated salt drinks can cause nausea, stomach cramps, and diarrhea, which is the opposite of what you want with a hangover. If you feel bloated, puffy, or more nauseated after LMNT, switch to plain water.

A rarer problem runs the other way. People who drink huge amounts of plain water quickly can dilute the sodium in their blood. That's one reason a moderate amount of electrolytes after heavy drinking and sweating is reasonable. The fix for either extreme is the same: drink steadily, not all at once, and don't overdo anything.

## LMNT Before, During, or After Drinking?

This is the second most common question about LMNT and alcohol. Here's how each timing plays out.

### Before you go out

Having a glass of LMNT before a night of drinking is a reasonable idea if you're going to be sweating, like at a festival, a hot outdoor event, or a long night of dancing. Starting out well hydrated helps. It won't stop you from getting drunk or prevent a hangover, and there is no good evidence that pre-loading electrolytes changes hangover severity. If you're going to a sit-down dinner, a regular glass of water does the same job.

### While you're drinking

Alternating alcoholic drinks with water is one of the simplest things that actually helps, mostly because it slows your drinking down. You don't need LMNT for this. Plain water is fine. If you're outside in the heat and sweating, an LMNT mixed in a large water bottle is a sensible way to replace some salt.

Don't mix LMNT into alcoholic drinks expecting it to cancel out the alcohol. It won't. It just makes a salty cocktail.

### Before bed

A glass of LMNT before bed after a heavy night is a popular habit. It's fine if you mix it well (32 ounces) and sip it rather than chugging. The downside is that a large drink before bed can wake you up to pee, and alcohol already wrecks sleep quality. Many people do better with a moderate glass of water before bed and the electrolytes in the morning.

### The next morning

This is the most useful time. You've lost fluid overnight, your mouth is dry, and you're likely a bit dehydrated. One stick in 32 ounces, sipped over an hour alongside food, is a sensible approach.

Our [guide to electrolytes before or after drinking](/never-hungover/electrolytes-before-or-after-drinking) covers timing in more detail for all the main brands.

## LMNT Flavors and Versions After Drinking

LMNT sells several lines. Here's how they fit after a night out.

- **Standard flavors (Citrus Salt, Raspberry Salt, Watermelon Salt, and others):** the default choice. Citrus is often the easiest on a queasy stomach.
- **Raw (unsweetened):** pure salt taste. Hard to drink plain, but some people add it to soup, broth, or a squeeze of lemon water.
- **Chocolate Salt and other seasonal flavors meant to be mixed into hot drinks:** you can stir it into hot water, but a hot, salty drink isn't everyone's idea of a hangover cure.
- **LMNT Sparkling (canned):** a ready-to-drink sparkling version. Some people find carbonation settles their stomach, others find it makes bloating worse. If your stomach is upset, start with the still version.

Some LMNT flavors and seasonal releases contain small amounts of caffeine or other add-ins. Check the label if you're sensitive to caffeine, since caffeine on top of a hangover can make a racing heart or jittery feeling worse.

## LMNT vs Other Hangover Drinks

Here's an honest comparison of how LMNT stacks up against the drinks people usually reach for. Figures are approximate per stick or standard serving, based on published labels.

| | Sodium | Sugar | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| LMNT (1 stick) | ~1,000 mg | 0 g | Heavy sweating, low-carb diets, people who want no sugar |
| Liquid I.V. (1 stick) | ~500 mg | ~11 g | General hangover rehydration, mild stomach upset |
| Pedialyte (1 liter, classic) | ~1,000 mg per liter | Some sugar | Vomiting, diarrhea, can't keep food down |
| Gatorade (20 oz) | ~270 mg | ~34 g | Mild dehydration when you also want calories |
| Coconut water (1 cup) | Low sodium, higher potassium | Some natural sugar | A light, natural option, though low in sodium |
| Plain water | None | None | Most people, most mornings |

**LMNT's strengths for a hangover:** no sugar, the most sodium per stick, a simple ingredient list, and easy to carry.

**LMNT's weaknesses for a hangover:** too salty for many people at the standard dilution, no sugar to help when you can't eat, more sodium than most people need on a quiet morning, and pricier than mixing your own.

If you're choosing between LMNT and Liquid I.V. specifically, our [LMNT vs Liquid IV comparison](/never-hungover/lmnt-vs-liquid-iv) goes through taste, cost, and which fits which situation. If you'd rather see all the main options side by side, our [electrolyte drinks for hangovers comparison](/never-hungover/electrolyte-drinks-for-hangover-compared) covers Pedialyte, Liquid I.V., DripDrop, LMNT, and others. And if Liquid I.V. is already in your cupboard, our guide to [Liquid I.V. for a hangover](/never-hungover/liquid-iv-for-hangover) covers how to use it.

## LMNT Pros and Cons for Hangovers

**Pros**

- High sodium helps you hold on to the water you drink, which is useful after heavy sweating or vomiting
- Zero sugar and almost no calories
- Includes some potassium and magnesium
- Simple, short ingredient list
- Portable sticks you can keep in a bag or car

**Cons**

- About 1,000 mg of sodium per stick, which is a lot for people with high blood pressure or kidney or heart problems
- Very salty at 16 ounces; many people need to dilute it further to tolerate it
- No sugar, so it won't help with low blood sugar or give you energy when you can't eat
- Addresses only the dehydration part of a hangover
- Costs noticeably more per serving than a homemade salt-and-sugar drink
- Sold mostly online and direct from the brand, so it's not always easy to grab at a corner store on a hangover morning

## A Simple Morning-After Plan That Includes LMNT

If you've decided LMNT is a good fit for you, here's a sensible routine.

1. **Start with a glass of plain water** as soon as you're up.
2. **Mix one LMNT stick into 32 ounces of water.** Citrus or Raspberry tends to go down easiest. Sip it over the next hour rather than drinking it all at once.
3. **Eat something.** Toast, eggs, fruit, oatmeal, or a banana. Food helps your blood sugar, gives your gut the carbohydrate LMNT doesn't have, and often settles nausea. Our guide to [eggs for a hangover](/never-hungover/eggs-for-hangover) explains why eggs are a popular choice.
4. **Go easy on caffeine.** One cup of coffee is fine for most people. Several cups on top of a hangover can make anxiety and a racing heart worse.
5. **If you need a painkiller, choose carefully.** Ibuprofen is harder on the stomach after drinking, and acetaminophen (Tylenol) is harder on the liver. Our [Tylenol and alcohol guide](/never-hungover/tylenol-and-alcohol) explains the risks.
6. **Rest.** Sleep after drinking is poor quality, and a nap does more for most hangovers than any drink.
7. **Stop at one or two sticks.** After that, plain water is enough.

For a broader look at getting fluids back without overdoing anything, see our guide to [how to rehydrate after drinking](/never-hungover/how-to-rehydrate-after-drinking).

## What About Magnesium in LMNT?

LMNT includes about 60 mg of magnesium per stick, which people sometimes point to as a hangover benefit. Alcohol does increase magnesium loss through urine, and people who drink heavily over long periods are more likely to be low in it.

That said, 60 mg is a modest amount, and there is no good evidence that the magnesium in an electrolyte drink makes a hangover noticeably better. It's a nice extra, not a reason to choose LMNT. If you're curious about magnesium and drinking more broadly, our [magnesium and alcohol guide](/never-hungover/magnesium-and-alcohol) covers what the research does and doesn't support.

## When to See a Doctor

Most hangovers are miserable but harmless, and they fade within a day. An electrolyte drink is fine for those. Some situations need more than a salty drink.

> **Get emergency help (call 911 in the US) if someone who has been drinking:** is confused or very hard to wake, is breathing slowly or irregularly, has blue-tinged lips or cold, clammy skin, has a seizure, or keeps vomiting while drowsy or not fully awake. These are signs of alcohol poisoning. Don't let them "sleep it off," and don't try to treat it with an electrolyte drink.

**See a doctor or urgent care if you:**

- Can't keep any fluids down for more than several hours
- Have signs of serious dehydration: very little or no urine, dark urine that doesn't lighten as you drink, a racing heart at rest, or dizziness or fainting when you stand up
- Have vomit with blood in it or that looks like coffee grounds
- Have severe stomach pain, especially pain that spreads to your back
- Have chest pain or an irregular heartbeat that doesn't settle
- Have a severe headache unlike your usual hangover headache, a stiff neck, or vision changes
- Still feel very unwell more than about 24 hours after your last drink

**A separate note for people who drink heavily most days.** If you drink a lot on a regular basis and notice shaking, sweating, anxiety, or a racing heart when you stop, that may be alcohol withdrawal rather than a hangover. Withdrawal can become dangerous, and it's not something to manage with electrolyte drinks at home. Talk to a doctor, who can help you stop safely.

## Can You Prevent the Dehydration Part Entirely?

You can reduce it. The most reliable ways are boring but effective:

- **Drink less, and drink slower.** Every drink adds to the fluid loss.
- **Alternate each alcoholic drink with a glass of water.** It slows your pace and keeps you topped up.
- **Eat before and while drinking.** Food in your stomach slows how fast alcohol reaches your bloodstream.
- **Watch the heat.** Outdoor drinking in summer, crowded venues, and dancing all add sweat loss on top of alcohol's effect. This is where an LMNT in a big water bottle earns its place.
- **Pick lower-strength drinks.** Lower-alcohol options mean less alcohol per hour for the same number of drinks.

For a full plan, our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) walks through what actually works.

## Where DHM Fits Alongside LMNT

LMNT addresses fluid and salt. It does nothing for how your body processes alcohol itself. That's the area some people look to DHM (dihydromyricetin) for. DHM is a compound from the Japanese raisin tree that has been studied for its effects on alcohol metabolism and the brain. Most of the research comes from animal and lab studies, and human data are still limited. It's promising, not proven, and there is no good evidence that DHM prevents hangovers in everyone or makes heavy drinking safe.

If you want to try it, many people take it with water before or while drinking and then use an electrolyte drink like LMNT the next morning, so the two cover different parts of the problem. Popular options include [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) and the budget-friendly [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20). Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers how much to take and when, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) compare the main brands. If you take prescription medicines, check with your doctor or pharmacist before adding any supplement.

## The Bottom Line

- LMNT can help with the dehydration part of a hangover, especially after heavy sweating or vomiting. It doesn't treat the rest of the hangover.
- Mix one stick into 32 ounces of water, sip it slowly, and eat something with it.
- With about 1,000 mg of sodium per stick, it's not a casual daily habit for people with high blood pressure, kidney disease, or heart problems. Talk to your doctor first if any of those apply to you.
- Lower-sodium or sugar-containing drinks like Liquid I.V. or Pedialyte may suit you better if you're nauseated, can't eat, or need to limit salt.
- If someone shows signs of alcohol poisoning, call 911. An electrolyte drink is not a treatment for that.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Does LMNT help with a hangover?**

It can help with the dehydration part. LMNT is a high-sodium, sugar-free electrolyte mix, and the salt helps your body hold on to the water you drink after alcohol has made you urinate more. It does nothing for poor sleep, nausea, inflammation, or the by-products of alcohol metabolism, so it eases some symptoms rather than curing the hangover.

**Should I drink LMNT before or after drinking alcohol?**

The morning after is usually the most useful time: one stick in 32 ounces of water, sipped with food. Before drinking only makes much sense if you'll be sweating heavily, such as at a hot outdoor event. There is no good evidence that taking electrolytes before drinking prevents a hangover.

**How many LMNT sticks can I have in a day after drinking?**

For most healthy adults, one stick is plenty for a hangover morning, and two spread out with lots of water is a reasonable upper limit. Each stick has about 1,000 mg of sodium, and US dietary guidelines suggest most adults stay under 2,300 mg a day. Several sticks in a short time can cause nausea, cramps, or diarrhea.

**Is LMNT safe if I have high blood pressure?**

Talk to your doctor first. One stick contains about 1,000 mg of sodium, which is a large share of the daily limit the American Heart Association recommends, especially for people with high blood pressure. The same goes for kidney disease, heart failure, or taking water pills or other medicines that affect sodium or potassium.

**Is LMNT better than Liquid I.V. for a hangover?**

It depends on your morning. Liquid I.V. has about half the sodium and some sugar, which helps absorption and gives you energy if you can't eat, so it suits most hangovers. LMNT suits people who sweated heavily, follow a low-carb diet, or want zero sugar. Neither one is a cure.

**Why does LMNT taste so salty?**

Because it is. One stick in 16 ounces of water is saltier than the World Health Organization's oral rehydration solution. Mixing it into a full 32 ounces makes it much easier to drink and gentler on an upset stomach, and you get more of the water you actually need.

**Can I mix LMNT with alcohol?**

You can, but it doesn't cancel out the alcohol or prevent a hangover. It just adds salt to your drink. A better approach is to alternate alcoholic drinks with water, and save electrolytes for when you're sweating heavily or for the next morning.

**When is a hangover too serious for an electrolyte drink?**

Get medical help if you can't keep fluids down for several hours, have very little or dark urine, faint or feel very dizzy on standing, vomit blood, or have chest pain or a severe headache unlike your usual one. If someone is confused, very hard to wake, breathing slowly, or having a seizure after drinking, call 911. Those are signs of alcohol poisoning.
